extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Indian Office officials / Indian agents preparing annual agency reports
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit evaluation criteria used in 19th-century United States Indian agency annual reports to assess tribal condition, administration, and outcomes (population, education, agriculture, policing, sanitation, transportation, stock-raising, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Population census and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of men, women, boys, and girls (present and absent) — detailed census figures to show total population and composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide tabulated counts (No. of men, women, boys, girls; total present and absent). Note absentees explicitly and account for causes of absence. Compare with prior years to detect change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population increase / decrease and causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure of tribal population change (e.g., 'these tribes have increased slightly the past year'), with attribution of causes such as return of prisoners or students returning from Carlisle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting increases or decreases, indicate specific causes (returns from confinement, educational returns, etc.) rather than just raw numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanence of residence and willingness to settle
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicators whether individuals or bands accept permanent residence on the reserve or 'cling to the belief that they will eventually be allowed to return' north.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence includes refusal to accept issued wagons or industries, reluctance to place children in school, verbal statements of intent, and retention of hopes to return to traditional lands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of civilizing advice and adoption of peaceful arts
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which a tribe 'have shown every desire to accept all the advice of the constituted authorities and to act in accordance with the wishes of the department' and progress in 'arts of peace and ways of civilization.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure by participation in construction, brick-making, lime-burning, mechanics' work, freighting, and other civil employment; by observable behavior changes and expressed desires for employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment and labor participation (Indian labor usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of Indian labor for agency projects and industry (who works, persistence, supervision needed), and the policy of employing Indians where capable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record number employed, types of tasks, tendencies (e.g., initial short-lived effort but increasing stamina over repeated attempts), need for daily supervision to ensure authorized workers are at work, and apprenticeship outcomes (Indians taking skilled posts after training).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation efficiency and freighting by Indians
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance of Indian freighting operations (timeliness, loss/theft rates), number of wagons issued, and tonnage transported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report whether supplies were promptly hauled, whether any package was lost or tampered with, number of wagons issued, and policy balancing wagons issued vs freight volume to avoid idle wagons that defeat enterprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indian police effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization and effectiveness of the Indian police in suppressing horse stealing and maintaining order ('almost total suppression of horse stealing'), and removal of intruders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document police organization (officers and men), outcomes (reduction in crimes), specific duties (removing intruders), and impact on reserve security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial and manual labor schools (education provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Existence and performance of manual labor and boarding schools (months operated, average scholars, 'progress made and results attained').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report average attendance, term length, qualitative progress, and the role of industrial education; include numbers sent to distant institutions like Carlisle and compare proportion of school-age children receiving instruction (e.g., 25% of eligible children).

rubrics_metrics.name: Missionary work outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Effectiveness of missionaries in education and industrial training under societies (e.g., Society of Friends, Mennonites), and plans for industrial schools and farms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note organization, societies involved, planned expansions (industrial school and farm), the missionaries' character (practical, earnest), and expected long-term results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanitary and public health indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical treatment performance and mortality ('comparatively little mortality'), prevalence of diseases (venereal, scrofulous), and changes in reliance on native medicine vs physician remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record number and severity of cases treated, mortality rates, trends (native medicine being combined with physician's remedies), identified public-health causes (venereal disease leading to scrofula), need for stringent measures, and adequacy of medical supplies (special requisitions to meet deficiencies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agricultural output and practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Acres broken and cultivated, yields per acre (e.g., 'yield will be about 12 bushels per acre'), crop conditions, and farming practices (fencing before breaking sod).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report acres cultivated, yields, effects of drought and insects, timing of breaking sod, and policies like refusing to turn sod until fenced with an eight-rail worm fence to protect crops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stock-raising and herd growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers and ownership of cattle (purchases, donations, natural increase), net increases (e.g., 'from 285 cattle ... a net increase of 305 in five years'), assignment of cattle to schools and Indians, and distribution policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide inventory counts, origin of stock (government purchase, penalty, donations), distribution method (to children, schools, pro rata), losses, and commentary on incentives/disincentives (small per-capita shares may not incentivize care).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hides and market effects on herds
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact of hide prices and trader purchases on incentives to keep cattle (traders forbidden to buy unbranded hides but Indians may still sell), and recommendation to keep trader hide prices reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how high hide prices may induce slaughtering cattle for immediate sale and recommend policy levers (price regulation, branding enforcement) to discourage depletion of herds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing construction and settlement evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent of house-building and settlement (few houses built historically; more expected as Indians devote ponies/labor to construction), indicating progress toward permanent homes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record number of houses made, trends in selling ponies to fund labor, and the relation between house-building and family/land settlement patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of agency consolidation and infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative effects of removal/consolidation (warehouse location, distance to rations, telegraph office establishment, need for bridge over Washita), and whether consolidation caused disruption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether consolidation has worked well, note logistical shortcomings (warehouse location across river causing high-water problems), and recommend infrastructure fixes (building a bridge) and track telegraph/communication improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Police organization structure and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition of police (e.g., '1 captain, 1 lieutenant, 4 sergeants, and 22 privates'), obedience, armament status, and assigned tasks (driving out cattlemen, hunting stray stock, messenger duties).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report rank-and-file numbers, obedience and discipline, timing of arms issuance, and concrete tasks performed and results achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of freighting by Indians versus contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparative success of Indian freighting vs contract freighting by whites ('has proved a perfect success' and 'not a single case... of a package being lost').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide direct comparisons of loss/theft, timeliness, accountability, and recommend continuation or expansion if Indians outperform contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rations adequacy and consumption behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequacy of issued rations, consumption patterns (ration consumed in ~4 days rather than a week), and consequences such as butchering cattle to fill gaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note ration insufficiency effects on nutrition and herd depletion, observe how lack of ration-management knowledge affects consumption, and suggest policy actions (ration sizing, education, price controls) to prevent adverse behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of citizen dress and cultural indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which Indians wear citizen's dress and live in houses as an indicator of assimilation/civilization ('number of Indians who wear citizen's dress has increased very much').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use change in clothing, housing, and cultivation behavior as qualitative markers of progress; report notable conversions among previously reluctant individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy to weaken tribal authority and promote individual settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative actions to 'destroy the tribal relations as much as possible' by allowing relatives to band together under appointed headmen, weakening chiefs' influence to promote settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document methods used (appointing headmen, suggesting relocations), observed outcomes (bands reduced in size, some appointed men becoming prominent), and link to objectives like encouraging permanent houses and independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limiting white employes and promoting apprenticeships
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy limiting white employees to mechanical and skilled labor while employing and apprenticing Indians where capable, with the goal that trained Indians eventually replace white men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report where Indians have been employed, apprenticeships assigned, and evidence of Indians later taking over positions formerly held by whites.
